=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
File: scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh
Line or code reference: lines 2132-2156 (the new scope-check block, immediately after `emit_conflict_resolver_substate "Failed" "${attempt}"; exit 78`)
Problem: The comment immediately above the new scope check reads "Check the attempt-relative tree even when the agent exited non-zero. The post-loop touched-set guard remains the final defense; this early check makes an out-of-scope edit retryable only after full restoration." However, the block is placed after the `exit 78` that fires on a non-zero agent exit. The check therefore only runs when the agent returned 0; the comment's "even when the agent exited non-zero" claim contradicts the placement.
Why it fails at runtime: A non-zero agent exit paired with out-of-scope edits (e.g. an agent that crashed mid-write after editing a path outside the conflicted set) skips the early scope check entirely. The diff exits 78 instead, so the broken working tree is left untouched and the post-loop guard at lines 2605-2626 only fires once the next call to `_restore_attempt_base` rebuilds from an allowlist snapshot that does not cover the out-of-scope edit. The README PR comment from a prior round claims the fix preserves `check_resolver_diff.sh` as the final defense, so the practical impact is small, but the comment misrepresents what the code actually does and will mislead the next reader about which paths the early check covers.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
